## data prep

the dataset is loaded and curred. We remove adult = 0 and NAs

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| results: hide
data250_afabae_00 <- read.csv("../../../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/02.aphis_fabae_on_faba_collection/aphis_fabae_fecundity_on_faba_collection_2024-04-02.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep = ",") %>%  
  mutate(ivip = as.factor(ivip)) %>% 
  mutate(session = as.factor(session)) 



data250_afabae_01 <- data250_afabae_00 %>% filter(!is.na(larvae_total_number))
data250_afabae_01$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_01$ivip)

data250_afabae_02<- data250_afabae_01 %>% filter(adult_alive != "0") #remove if no adult
data250_afabae_02$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_02$ivip)

data250_afabae_02$ivip <-as.factor(data250_afabae_02$ivip)




```

Once we have removed the NAs and all rows for which we don't have an adult, we can still make adjustments to the dataset. We can remove outliers to ensure that our distribution approaches a normal distribution, and we can also filter out genotypes based on a threshold for the minimum number of repetitions required to keep a genotype.

The goal of this script is to study how our model reacts to changes in the outlier removal rate and the minimum number of repetitions required to retain a genotype.

in the folowing loop we varry two parameters, i and x the coef of stringensy for the outliers removal and the minimal number of reps for the genotypes respectively.

when x = 1 we remove a lot of outlier and when x = 2 almost no outliers are removed

```{r}

# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
results <- data.frame(x = numeric(0), i = numeric(0), RMSE = numeric(0), 
                      n_before = numeric(0), n_after = numeric(0), n_diff = numeric(0), H2=numeric(0),shapiro=numeric(0),shapiro_res=numeric(0),NGEN=numeric(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through different values of x
for (i in 3:7) {
  ###filter based on IQR
    # Calculate IQR and bounds for outlier removal
    IQR_value <- IQR(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number)
    lower_bound <- quantile(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR_value
    upper_bound <- quantile(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR_value
    filter ="IQR"
    # Filter out outliers
    data <- data250_afabae_02[data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number >= lower_bound & data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number <= upper_bound, ]
    
    
    data <- data %>%
      group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
      filter(n() >= i) %>%             # Keep only groups with i or more repetitions
      ungroup() 
    
    
    data$ivip <- droplevels(data$ivip)
    
    NGEN<-nlevels(data$ivip)
    
   
    # Number of rows before removing outliers
    n_before <- nrow(data250_afabae_02)
    
    
    # Number of rows after removing outliers
    n_after <- nrow(data)
    
    # Calculate the difference in number of observations
    n_diff <- n_before - n_after
    
    # Fit the model
    mod <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ ivip + (1|session/block), data = data)
    
    # Extract fitted values and residuals
    fitted_values <- fitted(mod)
    residuals_values <- residuals(mod)
    
    # Perform the Shapiro-Wilk test
    shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(residuals_values)
    
    # Print the p-value (this is your quantification of normality)
    shapiro_res <- shapiro_result$p.value
    
    # Perform the Shapiro-Wilk test
    shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(data$larvae_total_number)
    
    # Print the p-value (this is your quantification of normality)
    shapiro <- shapiro_result$p.value
    
    # Calculate RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error)
    RMSE <- sqrt(mean(residuals_values^2))
    
    # Fit the model with a fixed formula
    mod_h2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | ivip) + (1 | session), data = data)
    
    # Get the variance components
    estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
    
    # Extract the relevant variance components
    genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
    residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]  # Adjust based on the placement of residual variance
    
    nbE <-nlevels(data$session)
    
    # Calculate heritability (h2)
    H2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))
    
    
    
    # Store the results in the data frame
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(filter = filter, i = i, RMSE = RMSE, n_before = n_before, n_after = n_after, n_diff = n_diff, H2 = H2, shapiro = shapiro, shapiro_res = shapiro_res, NGEN=NGEN))
}
```

Based on these first results it appears that IQR is the best filtering option. We still need to detremine the best value for i. For that we will use a similar loop with more repetitions to which we will add the nucleotid diversity.

```{r}
# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
results <- data.frame(x = numeric(0), i = numeric(0), RMSE = numeric(0), 
                      n_before = numeric(0), n_after = numeric(0), n_diff = numeric(0), H2=numeric(0),shapiro=numeric(0),shapiro_res=numeric(0),NGEN=numeric(0), pi_value=numeric(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


for (i in 2:9) {
  ###filter based on IQR
    # Calculate IQR and bounds for outlier removal
    IQR_value <- IQR(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number)
    lower_bound <- quantile(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR_value
    upper_bound <- quantile(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR_value
    filter ="IQR"
    # Filter out outliers
    data <- data250_afabae_02[data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number >= lower_bound & data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number <= upper_bound, ]
    
    
    data <- data %>%
      group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
      filter(n() >= i) %>%             # Keep only groups with i or more repetitions
      ungroup() 
    
    
    data$ivip <- droplevels(data$ivip)
    
    NGEN<-nlevels(data$ivip)
    
   
    # Number of rows before removing outliers
    n_before <- nrow(data250_afabae_02)
    
    
    # Number of rows after removing outliers
    n_after <- nrow(data)
    
    # Calculate the difference in number of observations
    n_diff <- n_before - n_after
    
    # Fit the model
    mod <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ ivip + (1|session/block), data = data)
    
    # Extract fitted values and residuals
    fitted_values <- fitted(mod)
    residuals_values <- residuals(mod)
    
    # Perform the Shapiro-Wilk test
    shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(residuals_values)
    
    # Print the p-value (this is your quantification of normality)
    shapiro_res <- shapiro_result$p.value
    
    # Perform the Shapiro-Wilk test
    shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(data$larvae_total_number)
    
    # Print the p-value (this is your quantification of normality)
    shapiro <- shapiro_result$p.value
    
    
    # Calculate RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error)
    RMSE <- sqrt(mean(residuals_values^2))
    
    # Fit the model with a fixed formula
    mod_h2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | ivip) + (1 | session), data = data)
    
    # Get the variance components
    estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
    
    # Extract the relevant variance components
    genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
    residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]  # Adjust based on the placement of residual variance
    
    nbE <-nlevels(data$session)
    
    # Calculate heritability (h2)
    H2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))
    
    vcf_samples <- colnames(vcf@gt)[-1]  # Exclude "FORMAT"
pheno_samples <- data$ivip  # Replace SampleID with your actual column name
samples_to_keep <- vcf_samples[vcf_samples %in% pheno_samples]
vcf@gt <- vcf@gt[, c("FORMAT", samples_to_keep)]  # Always keep the FORMAT column


# Convert to genlight (adegenet)
genlight_obj <- vcfR2genlight(vcf)


# Custom nucleotide diversity function:
nuc_div <- function(x) {
  x <- as.matrix(x)
  n <- nrow(x)
  p <- colMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE) / 2  # allele frequency (assuming 0/1/2 coding)
  pi <- 2 * p * (1 - p)
  mean(pi, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Apply to your data:
pi_value <- nuc_div(genlight_obj)
    
    # Store the results in the data frame
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(filter = filter, i = i, RMSE = RMSE, n_before = n_before, n_after = n_after, n_diff = n_diff, H2 = H2, shapiro = shapiro, shapiro_res = shapiro_res, NGEN=NGEN, pi_value=pi_value))
}
```

```{r}

ggplot(results, aes(x = i, y = NGEN)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,13,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,250)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = NGEN), arrow = T) +
  labs(x = "N biological replicates", y = "N genotypes") +
  ggtitle("N genotypes = f(N biological replicates)")

y<-as.vector(results$NGEN)
x<-as.vector(results$i)

# Compute slope (finite differences)
slope <- diff(y) / diff(x)

# To align slopes with x-values, use midpoints
x_mid <- (x[-1] + x[-length(x)]) / 2

# Plot slope (derivative)
plot(x_mid, slope, type = "b", col = "red", main = "Numerical Derivative (Slope)",
     ylab = "Slope", xlab = "x")
abline(h = 0, col = "gray", lty = 2)  # reference line for zero slope



```

It can be hard to read the relation between Genotype number and i. Therefore it is helpfull to plot the slop (the value is the difference between number of genotype beforre and after) based on the decrease in genotypes number we can choose 5 or 7 as the best i value.

```{r}

ggplot(results, aes(x = i, y = RMSE)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,13,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(9.15,9.85)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = NGEN), arrow = T) +
  labs(x = "i", y = "RMSE") +
  ggtitle("variation of RMSE depending on i")

y<-as.vector(results$RMSE)
x<-as.vector(results$i)

# Compute slope (finite differences)
slope <- diff(y) / diff(x)

# To align slopes with x-values, use midpoints
x_mid <- (x[-1] + x[-length(x)]) / 2

# Plot slope (derivative)
plot(x_mid, slope, type = "b", col = "red", main = "Numerical Derivative (Slope)",
     ylab = "Slope", xlab = "x")
abline(h = 0, col = "gray", lty = 2)  # reference line for zero slope


```

the lowest value for RMSE is with i=4. However base on the curve we could also be tempted to chosse a value of 7 for i.
